description: The line plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers of a neural network model, comparing four distinct components: `attn_output`, `attn_residual`, `ffn_output`, and `ffn_residual`. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the model’s layers. The y-axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” ranges from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200, indicating the magnitude of the highest activation observed per layer. The `ffn_residual` (solid red line) shows a sharp rise starting at layer 5, peaking near 1600 around layer 13, and then declining sharply after layer 20. The `attn_residual` (dotted orange line) follows a similar trajectory but with slightly lower peaks and a more gradual decline. The `ffn_output` (dash-dot green line) exhibits a spiky pattern, with a major peak near layer 5 (~1400), a smaller peak near layer 13 (~1000), and another near layer 22 (~1200). The `attn_output` (dashed blue line) remains near zero for most layers, with a modest rise only in the final layers, reaching about 200 at layer 23. The plot highlights the dominance of residual connections in activation magnitude compared to output components, particularly in the middle layers.
